Source-independent table structure

Source: R/TosiSchema.R
TosiStructure.Rd

TosiStructure describes a table or series through its ordered components, identifiers, labels, roles, and available value domains, without requiring source identity or a source version. It retains language, frequency, and series-key information. TosiSchema inherits this structure and adds a canonical source identity and version. Both classes support the same structural methods. Fields are read-only; direct and nested replacement fails. Use $column_names() to see the physical names for each column mode.

Use structure$as_schema(connector_id, object_id, data_version) to create a new source-bound schema. The receiver is unchanged and existing component instances are shared, not cloned. The inherited method on a bound schema also creates a new result with the supplied binding, without replacing the receiver's source binding.

Use schema$component(id) to obtain the existing component by its exact ID, and schema$domain_table(id) to inspect its complete domain. Every component also provides component$domain_table() with the same return contract. These methods preserve source order and vector types. Code domains contain code and, only when supplied, label; Time and Frequency domains contain time and frequency, respectively, retaining native Date and frequency values. An unrecorded domain returns NULL (including Value); a recorded empty domain returns a typed zero-row tibble. Domain inspection does not translate values into source filters; filter conventions are source-specific. Use print(schema) or schema$print() for a compact overview without domain values. Dimensions, Time, Frequency and unknown roles are shown together; Attributes and Value are summarized separately. Relative order within each group is preserved; the stored component order is unchanged. Domain sizes distinguish unrecorded from recorded empty domains. Each component supports print(component) and component$print(n = 3) for focused inspection. The per-call n bounds domain rows for Dimensions, Time, Frequency and unknown roles. Attributes show metadata and domain size only; Value shows its unit when recorded. Printing returns the same object invisibly without mutation. $domain_table() extracts the complete domain regardless of display limits. Display truncation and omission markers are not literal source-filter values. Use str(schema) or str(component) for structural R6 inspection, including fields and method signatures, rather than the interactive overview. Component constructors are technical exports, not an extension interface.

TosiStructure$new()

Construct a structural schema from package-owned schema components.

Usage

TosiStructure$new(
  components,
  object_type = NULL,
  lang = NULL,
  frequency = NULL,
  series_key = NULL
)

Arguments

components

Non-empty ordered list of package-owned schema component objects.

object_type

Optional connector-supplied object type: "table", "series", or NULL.

lang

Scalar natural-language code or "codes".

frequency

Optional scalar known frequency code.

series_key

Optional ordered character vector of eligible series-key component IDs.

Returns

A new TosiStructure object.

TosiStructure$as_schema()

Create a source-bound schema sharing the existing component instances. The receiver and its source binding, if any, remain unchanged.

Usage

Scalar canonical connector ID.

Scalar canonical object ID.

Returns

A new TosiSchema object.

TosiStructure$print()

Print a compact role-grouped overview of every component, without domain values or changing stored component order.

Usage

TosiStructure$print()

TosiStructure$component()

Look up a component by its exact ID, not a list name, label, role or position. An unknown ID raises a lookup error.

Usage

TosiStructure$component(id)

Arguments

id

Exact component ID.

Returns

The existing schema component object, without cloning.

TosiStructure$domain_table()

Return a component's complete domain by delegating to its $domain_table() method. An unknown ID raises a lookup error.

Usage

TosiStructure$domain_table(id)

Arguments

id

Exact component ID.

Returns

A tibble in source order with code and optional label, time, or frequency columns, preserving vector types. Returns NULL for an unrecorded domain, or a typed zero-row tibble for a recorded empty domain.

TosiStructure$column_names()

Return physical column names in component order without changing the structure. "labels" uses component labels, "safe_labels" converts them to safe IDs, and "ids" uses canonical component IDs. Label modes fall back to IDs with a warning when labels are blank, protect canonical Time and Value names, and repair collisions across the complete structure, including undelivered Attributes.

Usage

TosiStructure$column_names(col_mode = c("labels", "safe_labels", "ids"))

Arguments

col_mode

One of "labels", "safe_labels", or "ids".

Returns

A character vector of physical names named by component ID.
